reason: The Jan 2026 faster-switchover item and the Apr 2026 Blue/Green plus RDS Proxy item only strengthen the claim; no later item removes Proxy or smart driver support.
The RDS and Aurora user guides (fetched this month) both still say 15 months in the console and at least 465 days in the CLI and API; the PI end-of-life items do not change the create-time rule.

The CloudWatch Database Insights page is newer than the May 2025 PI end-of-life item (it states the July 31, 2026 end and the migration) and still gives 7 days included, 1-24 months in Standard at the Performance Insights price, and 1-24 months in Advanced at no extra cost.
The May 2026 launch item introduced this behavior and the user guide section matches it; later items concern instance classes only.
The charges page still lists upgrade and delete as the actions that stop the charge; the 2023-2024 Extended Support items precede it and no later item changes it.
The guide still uses this MySQL 5.7 example with February 29, 2024 and March 1, 2024; the later extension of 5.7 Extended Support to 2029 does not change these historical dates.
The What's New item extending MySQL 5.7 Extended Support to June 30, 2029 (from February 28, 2027) is already reflected in the claim, and Sept 2026 items still say up to three additional years.
The RDS FAQ and the billing guide Free Tier page both still give $100 in credits plus up to $100 more for activities, with the July 15, 2025 split; no later item changes it.
The 2022 'up to 50% faster' item is older than the guide, which says up to 2x and on by default for instance-store classes; the 2025-2026 items only add instance classes.
The supported-engines page still lists Db2 and Oracle as unavailable and no change item or corpus statement adds RDS Proxy support for them.
